findings.title: queued timestamp is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` once when the dataclass is defined, so every AssignmentSource created without an explicit queued value shares the same import-time timestamp instead of its creation time. If this field is later used for debugging, ordering, or expiring stale sync suppression, all records will appear to have been queued at process start. It should be `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: to_dict returns a non-JSON-serializable datetime used in Celery kwargs
findings.body: `to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)`, leaving `queued` as a datetime object. `sync_group_assignee_outbound` places that dict directly in `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs=...)`, whose arguments must survive task serialization; a raw datetime is not JSON-serializable and can make enqueueing the outbound assignee task fail in production (eager in-process tests would not expose this). Serialize `queued` to an ISO string in to_dict and parse it back in from_dict, with a round-trip test `from_dict(source.to_dict())`.

findings.title: assignment_source added to sync_status_outbound abstract instead of sync_assignee_outbound
findings.body: The new `assignment_source` parameter was added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound`, but no status caller passes it; meanwhile `sync_assignee_outbound` task (sync_assignee_outbound.py:59-61) now calls every installation as `sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)` while the abstract `sync_assignee_outbound` at line 397 still declares only `external_issue, user, assign=True, **kwargs`. Concrete providers that implement the abstract signature without **kwargs will raise TypeError when the task runs, breaking assignee sync for them. Add the parameter to the assignee abstract (and audit concrete implementations) instead of, or in addition to, the unused status one.
